0.0.n: Together with に, 別に softens the negative phrase: filming is not really necessary.

0.1.n: に combines with 別 to form 別に, which modifies the following negative phrase.

0.2.n: Negative て-form of 撮る; adding も makes an even-if-not condition.

0.3.n: After 撮らなくて, も indicates that not filming will not affect the result.

0.5.n: The platform name; the search location marker で is omitted in this casual sentence.

0.6.n: 探したら is the たら conditional form of 探す; its past-shaped ending does not mean past time here.

0.7.n: Indicates that many videos or results will appear, without naming them explicitly.

0.8.n: Polite form of 出る, used here for videos appearing in search results.

0.9.n: A sentence-ending particle that confidently offers information to the listener.

1.0.n: Shows that the speaker expects this result but is not completely certain.

1.1.n: Adds a friendly, conversational tone after 多分 and gently draws the listener in.

1.3.n: Names the search topic; no particular Chinatown is identified by this word alone.

1.5.n: The platform name, followed by で to indicate where the search happens.

1.6.n: Marks YouTube as the platform where the searching takes place.

1.7.n: The たら ending sets up a condition for the speaker’s video appearing.

1.9.n: 一番 strengthens 上, indicating the highest position in the search results.

1.10.n: Marks the position where the video appears: the top of the results.

1.11.n: Refers to the speaker; with の, it identifies whose video appears.

1.12.n: Links 私 to 動画 to show that the video belongs to the speaker.

1.13.n: Refers to the speaker’s video that appears in the search results.

1.14.n: Identifies 私の動画 as the thing that appears.

1.15.n: Plain form of 出る, used for appearing in search results rather than physically exiting.

2.0.n: Placed before 人気 to indicate the highest level of popularity.

2.1.n: A noun expressing popularity; 一番人気 describes something ranked highest in popularity.

2.2.n: Connects 一番人気 to 動画, making popularity a description of the video.

2.3.n: The speaker’s video is understood from the preceding sentence.

2.4.n: Marks the status in which the video appears, rather than a location or tool.

2.5.n: Polite form of 出る; the speaker switches from the plain ending used in the previous line.

0.lit: Even without particularly filming, if you search YouTube, plenty appear, you know.
0.tip: なくても means even if not; here it reassures the listener that filming is unnecessary.

1.lit: Probably, you know, Chinatown—if you search on YouTube, at the very top my video appears.
1.tip: 中華街 is the search topic, while YouTubeで tells you where to search.

2.lit: As the most popular video, it appears.
2.tip: で here means as, describing the status in which the video appears.
